problems.title: Fundamental Problems We Solve
problems.subtitle: From ex-post isolated snapshots to end-to-end trusted evidence, bridging the trust deficit in the AI era

cards.title: Overvaluing Outputs, Neglecting Process: Impossible Provenance
cards.painPoint: Only the final artifact hash is retained, discarding prompt deduction and human iterations; copyright and provenance disputes cannot be substantiated.
cards.solution: DAG evidence graphs capture the full causal chain of prompts, parameter derivations, human edits, and model versions.

cards.title: Vulnerable Text Logs: Blame Shifting and Tampering
cards.painPoint: Application logs and database records can be altered or erased by admins or attackers, lacking objective neutral self-proving authority.
cards.solution: Self-contained .aep cryptographic packages bound to authoritative timestamps and digital signatures; any tampering invalidates the proof instantly.

cards.title: Challenging Fact-Finding: High Judicial Admissibility Thresholds
cards.painPoint: Fragmented electronic evidence, screenshots, and plain texts are trivial to forge, severely hindering judicial and arbitral fact-finding.
cards.solution: Structured evidence aligned directly with electronic litigation preservation baselines; authoritative timestamps and chains flow straight into courtroom and arbitration.

about.title: About the Project
about.subtitle: AI Agent Evidence Infrastructure
about.problemDesc: Autonomous AI agents (Coding Agents, DevOps Agents, etc.) are executing mission-critical tasks such as code modification, infrastructure deployment, financial transactions, and automated approvals, exposing three core vulnerabilities: ① Accountability Black Box: Agents perform impactful actions (dropping tables, altering configs, deploying code, executing transfers) without tamper-proof audit trails, making it impossible to attribute whether human or AI acted, and upon which context; ② Vulnerability of Conventional Logs: Plain-text logs and database records can be easily modified or deleted by administrators or attackers, lacking objective cryptographic self-proving power; ③ Multi-Agent Collaboration Without Verifiable Proofs: Handoffs and decisions across upstream/downstream agents lack non-repudiation and unforgeable digital signatures.
about.valueDesc: AEP packages agent actions and resulting artifacts into cryptographically verifiable structured evidence containers (.aep). Anyone holding an evidence package can independently verify the execution identity, causal order, and immutable integrity without relying on centralized servers — delivering an ironclad Proof of AI Action.
about.visionDesc: AEP provides a comprehensive trusted infrastructure services matrix for autonomous AI: AEP PKI establishes machine identity credentials (Who), AEP TSA locks reliable causal sequencing (When), and AEP Chain anchors global immutable finality (Immutability). With Evidence MCP as the native core integration gateway, AEP covers the full lifecycle from action capture and notarization to independent verification and neutral audit.
about.matrixBadge: Cloud Trusted Services Matrix · TRUST SERVICES
about.pkiTitle: AEP PKI (Machine Identity & Digital Certificate Service)
about.pkiDesc: Machine identity network and digital certificate infrastructure, assigning independent cryptographic credentials and certificate chains to each AI Agent to solve the Who problem and guarantee non-repudiation.
about.tsaDesc: High-precision causal time sequencing and RFC 3161 trusted timestamp receipts, solving the When problem by proving actions existed prior to specific points in time without backdating risk.
about.chainDesc: Distributed blockchain ledger and zero-knowledge public existence anchoring, solving the Immutability problem by anchoring evidence root digests publicly to guarantee immutable finality.

protocol.title: Protocol Specification
protocol.subtitle: An open, cryptographically verifiable, and extensible evidence protocol for AI agents
overview: AEP (Attestation & Evidence Exchange Protocol) is an open evidence infrastructure protocol built specifically for AI agents.
The core problem it solves: in an autonomous agent era, how to prove which agent executed a critical action, when it happened, and whether the context and execution remain intact and untampered.
Through digital certificates, causal time proofs, and global ledger anchoring, AEP establishes a transparent and neutrally auditable evidence chain for independent verification across the web.

protocol.levelsSubtitle: From L0 to L7, evidence strength increases progressively (cumulative)

levels.desc: PlainHash: any valid package payload (unsigned hash)
Signed: at least one valid asymmetric signature
Identity-verified: identity verified via CA/IdP certificate chain
Anchored: distributed global ledger existence anchoring
Notarized: endorsement by a neutral audit or attestation authority
Continuously-witnessed: continuous lifecycle execution records with multi-party consensus witnessing
Hardware-rooted: TEE / secure enclave hardware root of trust

protocol.levelsStatus: Current Engineering Status: L0–L4 (Hash, Signature, Identity/Witness, Timestamp TSA, Blockchain Anchor Chain) are fully implemented and production-ready; L5–L7 are reserved for advanced protocol evolution.

standards.title: Evidence MCP
standards.desc: MCP is the de facto standard for agent-tool interaction; AEP treats Evidence MCP as a native core integration gateway to empower agents with native evidence capabilities.

standards.title: C2PA
standards.desc: C2PA focuses on media content provenance (Content Credentials), while AEP concentrates on verifiable evidence chains across the full lifecycle of AI agent executions. The two are complementary.

standards.title: W3C PROV
standards.desc: PROV provides a general provenance ontology specification. AEP's evidence graph closely aligns with its data model while being cryptographically optimized for AI behaviors.

architecture.dataflowSubtitle: Complete closed loop from action capture to independent verification
dataflowSteps: AI Agent executes mission-critical tasks and triggers action capture
Evidence MCP captures and standardizes Artifacts and Events
Compute cryptographic hash digests of artifacts and events
Generate asymmetric digital signatures using agent private key
Build causal graphs and construct Merkle integrity proofs
Seal and package into standardized .aep evidence container
Any third party verifies independently offline or online
architecture.packageDesc: The .aep evidence package is a standardized, out-of-the-box container hermetically sealing manifest specifications, identity metadata, artifact digests, causal event chains, Merkle proofs, and digital signatures.

security.title: Security Model
security.subtitle: Zero-trust security based on cryptographic verifiability
modelText: AEP's security design centers on one core philosophy: providing an objective, verifiable evidence infrastructure rather than subjectively endorsing the veracity of content conclusions. The protocol assumes no centralized trust, but enables any entity to objectively audit and trace an Agent's identity, timestamp window, and data integrity independently of the execution environment.

All security properties are grounded in rigorous asymmetric cryptography, collision-resistant hashing, Merkle tree proofs, and RFC 3161 timestamping mechanisms, making unauthorized alterations or forgeries cryptographically undeniable.

crypto.title: SM2 / Asymmetric Digital Signatures
crypto.desc: Discrete logarithm and elliptic curve cryptography for execution identity authenticity and non-repudiation

crypto.title: SM3 / Cryptographic Hash Algorithm
crypto.desc: 256-bit secure hash digest guaranteeing avalanche-effect integrity verification across all inputs

crypto.title: Merkle Tree Existence Proofs
crypto.desc: Efficient proof of membership supporting high-throughput independent verification of large-scale action records

crypto.title: AEP TSA Trusted Timestamp
crypto.desc: High-precision causal time sequencing (RFC 3161) eliminating backdating and replay risks

threats.desc: Malicious actors altering notarized agent code, decisions, or outputs
threats.mitigation: Cryptographic hash + Merkle tree: any single-bit modification causes an avalanche root mismatch, failing verification immediately

threats.desc: Forging agent credentials to produce counterfeit evidence
threats.mitigation: AEP PKI certificate chains and private key signing: private keys are held exclusively, allowing verifiers to expose forgeries instantly

threats.desc: Replaying stale evidence or manipulating causal event sequencing
threats.mitigation: Monotonically increasing sequence numbers coupled with AEP TSA timestamp proofs establish a strict causal closed loop

flowSteps.desc: Deconstruct .aep container hierarchy, validate directory specs, and enforce path-traversal protection
Extract object topology, construct causal graphs, and enforce directed acyclic properties
Strictly validate schema compliance and field correctness of events, artifacts, and metadata
Independently recompute Merkle root hashes to verify dataset integrity and consistency
Validate asymmetric signatures and validity against public keys and AEP PKI certificate chains
Evaluate cryptographic assurance and external anchoring state to determine evidence level (L0–L7)
Generate machine-readable structured audit reports (supporting JSON / SARIF / HTML)

statements: AEP provides neutral, cryptographic evidence infrastructure: evidence is independently verifiable, transparently traceable, and fully auditable across its lifecycle.
Security relies on modern public-key cryptography and hash collision resistance; signature forgery and hash inversion are computationally infeasible.
Agent private key and certificate lifecycle management are foundational; securing private keys is essential for non-repudiation.
AEP focuses on the chain of evidence (Proof of AI Action), making all unauthorized modifications and impersonations mathematically detectable.
